The Heritage Committee in Israel has been working for the past several years to ensure that the U.S. government recognizes the heritage of the Israelites. The Committee is also involved with the establishment of the Israel Institute, a Center for Holocaust Studies, which promotes and researches the historicity of Holocaust and Genocide. It was founded by Rabbi Shlomo Zalman (the founder of the Temple Service Institute), Director of the National Museum of Jewish History in Jerusalem and Chancellor of the Faculty of Art and Design at Tel Aviv University. The institute’s mission includes collecting materials and teaching courses on the history of Jewish art and architecture. In addition, the group developed a curriculum for children and adults from kindergarten through grade four. The Museum was opened to the public on December 14, 2011.

Kowalski has a group of students explore the different stages of reef development in an effort to understand how reef building and the processes that drive it happen. She’s excited to be able to take your snorkel diving class with her!
The program is taught by a naturalist who explains why reef builders are important for the marine environment and how they shape our oceans. The class will include hands-on activities that promote underwater photography and underwater videos.
During the last two years, Dr. Kowalski and other scientists have been working on some very exciting projects:
• Studying coral growth and reproduction.
• Developing new materials for constructing artificial reefs.
• Understanding how coral reefs work.
• Identifying corals from rock samples.
• Finding patterns of algae growing at reef levels.
In addition to learning about the ocean, students learn about how ecosystems form and function, as well as how these systems affect climate and biodiversity. This class is designed to help students develop their skills in communication. The class includes a set of 10 PowerPoint slides so you can see what happens during each one.
